newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-BRUGES, GENK ARE EARLY LEADERS IN BELGIUM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRUGES, GENK ARE EARLY LEADERS IN BELGIUM.

text.p: Champions Lierse dropped a point in a lacklustre 1-1 draw with cup winners Germinal Ekeren in the Belgian first division on Sunday.

But last season's runners-up Club Bruges, minus Croatian striker Robert Spehar who last week joined Monaco in a deal worth over $5 million, maintained their 100 percent start to the new season, beating newly-promoted Westerlo 3-1.
Bruges trail high-scoring Genk on goal difference after two matches.

Despite going ahead after a penalty taken by their goalkeeper, Standard Liege lost 2-1 at Charleroi. Three players in that ill-tempered match were sent off, bringing the weekend's total to 10 dismissals in nine games.
On Saturday, pre-season favourites Anderlecht, reduced to 10 men after Spira Grujic was dismissed, slumped to a shock 2-0 home defeat against Brussels neighbours RWD Molenbeek.

But that result may not stand as Molenbeek made four substitutions during the match. Only three replacements are allowed. The league will look into the case and could order a re-match or award the game to Anderlecht.

Bottom club Lokeren provided the first managerial casualty of the season, sacking coach Fi Vanhoof after just one match. His successor Rudi Cossey fared little better -- Lokeren were thrashed 5-1 by Genk in his first game in charge on Saturday.
